answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by tying transaction limits to a staked work history, not to identity claims. Each agent locks a refundable deposit and completes verified tasks before its cap rises; its record follows it like a voyage log, and honest behavior cannot be faked overnight. A ferrous rule applies: a fresh identity resets the cap to zero, so an attacker wanting a thousand credible voices must fund a thousand deposits and pay for a thousand histories — a linear cost, while honest agents reuse one relic of proven work, their record, for free.
